item.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erdos conjecture
item.description: El-Zahar and Erd\H{o}s asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors… — Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: A resolution of the Erdos similarity problem in the large
item.description: We show that for every unbounded set $A\subset\mathbb R$ and every $0<\varepsilon<1$, there exists a closed set $S\subset\mathbb R$ that has measure at least $1-\varepsilon$ in every unit interval and contains no nontrivial affine copy of $A$. Moreover, $S$ can be chosen so that $|S\cap[x,x+1]|\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. This resolves the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem in the large. — Chi Hoi Yip — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT / RA / AC

item.title: Asymptotics of the three-color Hadwiger-Ramsey numbers
item.description: The Hadwiger-Ramsey number $R_h(k;\ell)$ is defined as the smallest integer $n$ such that for any edge coloring of a complete graph on $n$ vertices in $\ell$ colors at least one of the color classes induces a graph with a $K_k$ minor. We show that $R_h(k;3) = \left(β^{-1} + o(1)\right)k \sqrt{\ln k}$, where $β^{-1} = 2/\sqrt{-\ln(10-4\sqrt6)} = 1.58149\ldots$. This resolves the first open case of a problem by Axenovich and Steiner, who determined the asymptotic behavior of $R_h(k;2)$ and asked about the… — Sergey Norin, Neil Rahman — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Connectivity of Matroids with Breadth-Critical Tangles
item.description: We construct an explicit infinite sequence of nonnegative integers $(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ such that, for every $k\ge2$, every finite matroid with a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. The constants $s_i$ depend only on $i$. This proves a conjecture of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle. — Zhuo Li, Zhen Chen — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
item.description: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erd\H{o}s (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $\Omega(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstra\"{e}te (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. It is… — Bing Wei, Haidong Wu, Shunzhe Zhang — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: Matroid Connectedness and Component Decomposition: Breaking the Quadratic Barrier
item.description: Deciding whether a matroid is connected and computing its connected components are two fundamental algorithmic problems in matroid theory. Since the 1970s, the best known algorithms for both problems have used $O(n^2)$ independence queries on an $n$-element ground set. Our main contribution is to break this quadratic barrier: we give a deterministic algorithm that computes all connected components of a matroid on $n$ elements with $O(n \log{n})$ independence queries. Our algorithm for component decomposition… — Manuel Aprile, Roberto Ronco — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: A Lower Bound for the Chromatic Number of Ball-Packing Graphs
item.description: For every odd prime power $q$, we construct a finite packing of congruent balls in dimension $d=q^2-q+1$ whose contact graph requires at least $2d$ colors. Consequently, the ball-packing chromatic number satisfies $\chiball(q^2-q+1)\ge2(q^2-q+1)$, and the same lower bound holds for congruent-ball packings. The construction starts from the complements of Hubaut's $C_{20}$ graphs and uses their Taylor extensions. We give an explicit finite-field adjacency rule for the $q^3$-vertex graph $H_q$, prove its strong… — Dan Ismailescu, Sunwoo Lee, Terry Lee — arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.DM / cs.CC / cs.DS

item.title: Non self-similar solutions to the Ricci flow coming out of metric cones
item.description: Given an asymptotically conical unstable expanding gradient Ricci soliton, we provide the existence of a family of Ricci flows starting at the same metric cone up to isometry. Moreover, the family of solutions we construct is shown to be parametrized by positive modes of the weighted Lichnerowicz operator associated to the background expanding gradient Ricci soliton. Each solution of this family is shown not to be induced by an expanding gradient Ricci soliton. If the background expander has no non-trivial… — Alix Deruelle, Tristan Ozuch, Felix Schulze — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Forbidden subset sums in a linear range: an inverse theorem and the Erdős-Graham irregularity problem
item.description: For $c>0$ let $f_c(n)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,\lfloor cn\rfloor\}$ such that $n$ is not a sum of distinct elements of $A$. Erdős and Graham asked whether $f_c(n)$ depends on $n$ in an irregular way (Erdős Problem \#361). We prove that $f_c(n)=\lfloor cn\rfloor-\lceil n/2\rceil$ for $c\ge 1$, while for $00$, then every $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,E\}$ with $|A|\ge E/q+\varepsilon T$ has a subset summing to $sT$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $T$ and all $E\le sT/2^{q-2}$. For $s=2$, this… — Mateo Matijasevick — arXiv: lean

item.title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests, cycles and complete bipartite graphs
item.description: For a graph $G$ and $m\ge2$ dividing $e(G)$, the zero-sum Ramsey number $R(G,\mathbb Z_m)$ is the least $N$ such that every $\mathbb Z_m$-labeling of $E(K_N)$ contains a copy of $G$ whose edge labels sum to zero. We disprove the Bialostocki--Dierker asymptotic conjecture for forests by constructing trees for every sufficiently large edge count whose ratio of zero-sum to two-color Ramsey numbers has lower limit at least $554/553>1$. For powers of two $q\ge2$, we characterize all $s,k\ge1$ satisfying… — Linlin Wang, Guoqing Wang — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Composite witness sieves, Kneser--Plancherel containers, and the exponent $5/7$ for the Erdős--Straus conjecture
item.description: For the Erdős--Straus equation $4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$, Vaughan's unconditional bound on the exceptional set $E(N)$ has stood at $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c(\log N)^{2/3})$ since 1970. We harness composite divisor witnesses at growing depth to cross this $2/3$ barrier unconditionally. On the full exceptional set $E(N)$, we prove the unconditional bound $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c'(\log N)^{5/7}/(\log\log N)^{2/7})$, improving the exponent to $5/7$ (with an intermediate stage at $7/10$). On the structured component… — Benjamin Dahan — arXiv: kakeya

item.title: Rational Turán exponents of a single $k$-uniform hypergraph
item.description: For a fixed $k$-uniform hypergraph $F$, let $\mathrm{ex}_k(n,F)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $F$-free $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. We prove that for every integer $k\ge2$ and every rational $r\in[0,1]$ there exists a $k$-uniform hypergraph $F_{k,r}$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathrm{ex}_k(n,F_{k,r})=Θ(n^{k-r}). \end{equation*} The case $k=2$ is the rational exponents conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits \cite{Erdos1988}, also known as Erdős problem \#571 \cite{BloomErdoswebsite}; a proof… — Chang Liu, Jue Dai — arXiv: lean

item.title: The $(t-1)$-chromatic Ramsey number of cycles for three colours
item.description: For integers $t\ge 2$ and $\ell\ge 3$, let $R^t_{t-1}(C_\ell)$ be the least integer $n$ such that every colouring of the edges of $K_n$ with $t$ colours contains a cycle of length $\ell$ whose edges use at most $t-1$ colours. Bucić and Khamseh determined the analogous number for paths and asked for its value for cycles. We answer this question for three colours: we show that $R^3_2(C_\ell)=\ell+\lfloor(\ell+1)/6\rfloor$ for every $\ell\ge 11$, and we determine the values for $3\le \ell\le 10$. — Amir Khamseh, Mohammad Hassan Safareh — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph
item.description: In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph. By defining the blue graph as the complement of the red graph, we utilize a specific join graph structure \(K_{9,9}… — Yuan Si — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Off-Diagonal Induced Ramsey Numbers
item.description: Given graphs $F$ and $H$, the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H)$ is the smallest integer $n$ for which there exists a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices such that every red-blue colouring of $E(G)$ contains either a blue induced copy of $F$ or a red induced copy of $H$. A conjecture of Kohayakawa, Prömel and Rödl asserts that, for every fixed graph $F$, this number is polynomial in $v(H)$. We prove this conjecture, showing that there is an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $$r_{\mathrm{ind}}(F,H) \leq… — Bruno Andrades, Marcelo Campos, Rafael Filipe, Anastasiia Kats — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: On knotted self expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\R^3$
item.description: In this article we produce many examples of knotted self expanders. For example, there is an expander isotopic to a trefoil knot with three half cylinders attached. — Alexander Mramor, Shengwen Wang — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Erdős--Straus Conjecture: Modular Inversion in Mordell Classes
item.description: We examine modular inversion of strict Grid certificates in a ceiling continued-fraction construction for the Erdős--Straus equation. The six Mordell classes modulo $840$ form four inversion orbits. Prime-input pattern frequencies in the pairs $121 \leftrightarrow361 $ and $289 \leftrightarrow 529$ have equal asymptotic limits for every fixed cutoff. — Andres Ventas — arXiv: modularity

item.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemerédi
item.description: Let $A(x)=|A\cap[1,x]|$. For every integer $h\ge3$, every finite $B_h$ set $A_0\subseteq\mathbb N$, and every $0 — Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang — arXiv: modularity

item.title: The three-colour bipartite Ramsey number of sufficiently long even cycles
item.description: For a bipartite graph $H$, let $\operatorname{br}_3(H)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every three-colouring of $K_{N,N}$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{br}_3(C_{2n})=3n$ for all sufficiently large $n$, and give the lower bound for every $n\ge2$. For the upper bound, we reduce a counterexample to a finite rational weighted profile. Cycle extension and vertex-cover arguments force the critical components to have six unique minimum covers which partition the profile. The… — Jiangdong Ai, Yihan Yin — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Proof of the Erdős-Szemerédi sunflower conjecture
item.description: In the 1970s, Erdős and Szemerédi conjectured that for any $n \ge k-1\ge 2$, any collection of subsets of $[n]$ not containing a $k$-sunflower has size at most $c_k^n$ for some $c_k<2$. In the $k=3$ case, this follows from the work of Croot, Lev, and Pach and Ellenberg and Gijswijt on the cap-set problem, through a reduction due to Alon, Shpilka, and Umans. We prove the conjecture for every $k \ge 3$. — Matija Bucić, Fankang He, Hyunwoo Lee — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: A polynomial method over formal power series
item.description: We give new upper bounds on families of integer vectors with prescribed coordinate multiplicities and a forbidden scalar product. Our method uses coefficient functions over formal power series and recovers the Frankl--Wilson bound for binary vectors. For vectors in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$, we obtain an exponential improvement over the ordinary polynomial count in a wide range; in certain regimes, we determine the lower limit of the exponential base. We use the new bounds to make progress on several questions in… — Artur Akhiiarov, Mikhail Koshelev, Andrey Kupavskii, Andrei Raigorodskii — arXiv: additive

item.title: Genus Increase in Closed Mean Curvature Flows
item.description: We construct closed mean curvature flows with arbitrarily large genus increase in every smooth Riemannian three-manifold, giving counterexamples to Ilmanen's genus-reduction conjecture. We prove that a compact hypersurface with a single isolated conical singularity and a power rate of convergence to its cone admits a mean curvature flow whose forward rescaled limit is a prescribed expander in the tangent space at the singular point, smoothly asymptotic to that cone. Combining this theorem with closed mean… — Jingwen Chen — arXiv: ricci

item.title: The 3-Color 2-Chromatic Gallai-Ramsey Number for Complete Graphs
item.description: For $1\le i\le j\le k$, let $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ be the least $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that every rainbow triangle-free $3$-coloring of $K_n$ (using red, blue, and green) contains a red/blue $K_i$, a red/green $K_j$, or a blue/green $K_k$. In this paper, we completely evaluate $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ for all values of $i$, $j$, and $k$ in which $r(K_i,K_j)$ is known. — Mark Budden, Elijah DeJonge — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Instability of mean curvature flow in expander coordinates
item.description: We study rotationally symmetric graphical solutions to mean curvature flow that are initially close to a homothetic reference expander, in particular near infinity. Based on a computer algebra aided proof, we show that under appropriate conditions, at large times, the solutions are closer to a different expander than to the reference expander. — Ben S. Lambert, Oliver C. Schnürer — arXiv: ricci

item.title: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers for 3-uniform tight hypergraph cycles
item.description: Let $C^{(3)}_n$ be the $3$-uniform tight cycle on $n$ vertices, that is, the $3$-uniform hypergraph on a cyclically ordered set of $n$ vertices whose edges are precisely the triples of consecutive vertices in the given cyclic order. We asymptotically determine the off-diagonal Ramsey numbers of $3$-uniform tight cycles. This is an off-diagonal analogue of a result of Haxell, Łuczak, Peng, Rödl, Ruciński and Skokan [Combin.\ Probab.\ Comput.\ 18 (2009), no.\ 1-2, 165--203] on the diagonal Ramsey numbers of… — Eng Keat Hng — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: An upper bound of 60 for the Ramsey number R(3,3,3,3)
item.description: We improve the upper bound on the classical Ramsey number $R(3,3,3,3)$ from 62 to 60. The proof is based on a global incidence count, classifications of small neighborhoods and exhaustive SAT computations. We formalize the mathematical reductions in Lean and refute every resulting formula with two SAT solvers. — Milos Tatarevic — arXiv: lean / arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
item.description: For $n,r\in\mathbb{N}$ with $r\geq 3$ and an $r$-graph (i.e., an $r$-uniform hypergraph) $H$, the Ramsey number $R(H,n)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}$ such that every red/blue coloring of the hyperedges of the $N$-vertex complete $r$-graph $K_N^{(r)}$ contains either a red copy of $H$ or a blue copy of $K_n^{(r)}$. For every integer $r\geq 3$, we characterize all $r$-graphs $H$ for which $R(H,n)$ is polynomial in $n$. Explicitly, we prove a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu… — Lior Gishboliner, Sepehr Hajebi, Xiangyu Li — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: A Computer-Assisted Proof that R(5,10;5,8)=21 for the Generalized Threshold Ramsey Number
item.description: We prove that the generalized threshold Ramsey number R(5,10;5,8) equals 21. This number corresponds to the set Ramsey number r_5(10,8) introduced by Harborth. The proof is computer-assisted. We first enumerate all (4,6;5,8)-good and (5,10;4,4)-good graphs. Then we apply the lucky-vertex inequality derived from the McKay--Radziszowski edge identity to filter candidate pairs for a gluing search, and encode the remaining cases as SAT instances. The search yields exactly 17 non-isomorphic (5,10;5,8;20)-good graphs… — Wancai Guo, Min Wan — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Prömel-Rödl Conjecture
item.description: The induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)$ is defined as the minimum order of a graph $F$ such that any 2-coloring of its edges with red and blue leads to either a red induced copy of $G$ or a blue induced copy of $H$. In 1998, Kohayakawa, Prömel, and Rödl conjectured that for any fixed graph $G$, there exists a constant $f=f(G)$ such that the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G, H)$ is bounded by $|V(H)|^f$ for every graph $H$. In this paper, we completely solve the Kohayakawa--Prömel--Rödl… — Chuang Zhong, Masaki Kashima, Yaping Mao — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: A note on the logarithmic exponent of Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
item.description: In this short note, we point out that the recent lower bounds for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers $r(s,t)$ with fixed $s\ge 5$, together with the recent proof of the Ajtai--Erdős--Komlós--Szemerédi independence conjecture, imply \[ r(4,t)=\frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}. \] This note is solely for informal circulation and will not be submitted for publication. — Kaizhe Chen — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Size Ramsey numbers of star forests with two components on one side
item.description: We determine the size Ramsey number of a two-component star forest versus an arbitrary star forest. Let $q,a,b,n_1,\ldots,n_q$ be positive integers with $a\ge b$ and $n_1\ge\cdots\ge n_q$. We prove that \[ \begin{split} \rhat\left(K_{1,a}\sq K_{1,b}, \bigsqcup_{i=1}^{q}K_{1,n_i}\right) ={}&(a+n_1-1) +\sum_{i=1}^{q-1}\max\{a+n_{i+1}-1,b+n_i-1\}\\ &+(b+n_q-1). \end{split} \] This proves the conjecture of Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp (Erdős Problem~\#561) in the case where one of the two star forests… — Chunlin You — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Attention-Graph Curvature for the Verification of Mathematical Reasoning
item.description: Language models have recently solved open Erdős problems and achieved gold-medal level performance on International Mathematical Olympiad problems. But their solutions, written in natural language, cannot yet be verified by proof assistants. An erroneous reasoning step can invalidate every step that comes after, so it is advantageous to detect errors early. Several methods have been proposed to detect erroneous reasoning quickly based on the features of the forward pass of the language model that performs… — Kanghyeon Kim, Johannes F. Lutzeyer, Yanzhu Guo — arXiv: llm math

item.title: Approximating Independent Sets Using Additive Combinatorics
item.description: We give a deterministic quasi-polynomial time algorithm for approximating the largest independent set in a graph. We show that if an $N$-vertex graph contains an independent set of size $2^{-t} N$, then we can find an independent set of size $2^t$ in quasi-polynomial time, for all $t$ up to a constant factor of $(\log N)^{1/3}$. This gives an approximation factor of $N / \exp((\log N)^{1/3})$, which has the same shape as known hardness results for quasi-polynomial time algorithms, up to a different exponent of… — Shachar Lovett — arXiv: additive

item.title: On the Erdős--Odlyzko--Sárközy conjecture for prime-power moduli
item.description: Erdős, Odlyzko and Sárközy conjectured that every reduced residue class modulo $q$ contains a product of two primes not exceeding $q$. O. Klurman, A. P. Mangerel and J. Teräväinen (2023) have shown that three primes suffice when $q$ is sufficiently smooth. We study the moduli $q=p^γ$ that are powers of a fixed prime $p$ and we show that the third prime can be taken subpolynomially small. For any $q_\bullet\le q$ for which $q_\bullet\ge\exp\bigl(C(\log q)^{2/3}(\log\log q)^{4/3}\bigr)$, we give an asymptotic… — William Banks, Igor E. Shparlinski — arXiv: riemann

item.title: An $8+9$ gluing computation for the Ramsey number $R(F_3,F_4)$
item.description: Let $F_t$ be the graph consisting of $t$ triangles with a common vertex and otherwise disjoint vertices. We prove that $R(F_3,F_4)=17$ using an $8+9$ gluing computation. Neighbourhood matching arguments give degree and clique restrictions that reduce the search on seventeen vertices to $88,294,674$ ordered seed pairs. The verified main computation excludes $88,294,634$ pairs. A cross-edge counting argument excludes thirty-four of the forty exceptional pairs, and independently checked finite-domain certificates… — Hanxin Jiang, Zehui Shao — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: 3SUM Is Really Hard: A Real-to-Integer Reduction
item.description: We show that if the 3SUM problem on integer-valued inputs can be solved in truly subquadratic time, then it can also be solved in truly subquadratic time on real-valued inputs. This answers an open problem posed by Chan, Vassilevska Williams, and Xu [STOC 2022], and constitutes the first such tight real-to-integer self-reduction in fine-grained complexity. Our proof relies on a surprising combination of the Frank--Tardos theorem from optimization with Freiman-type theorems from additive combinatorics. — Nick Fischer, Adam Polak, Jonas Schmidt — arXiv: additive

item.title: New bounds for off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey numbers
item.description: We study a conjecture of Conlon, Fox, Gunby, He, Mubayi, Suk, Verstraëte, and Yu, which characterizes the $3$-graphs $H$ for which the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(H,n)$ is polynomial. We prove the conjecture for $3$-graphs with at most five tight components. Additionally, we show that the full conjecture is equivalent to its specialization to linear $3$-graphs. We prove quasipolynomial upper bounds for a class of `forward-doubleable' $3$-graphs, which includes the Fano plane. Finally, we give an exponential… — David Conlon, Xiaoyu He, Jiaxi Nie, Logan Post — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: The $k$-color poset Ramsey number of the diamond is $2k$
item.description: The $k$-color Ramsey number of a poset $P$ is the smallest dimension $d$ such that any $k$-coloring of the $d$-dimensional Boolean lattice contains a monochromatic induced copy of $P$. For $ j\ge 2$ the $j$-diamond is the poset that consists of a maximum element, a minimum element and an antichain of size $j$. We prove that the $k$-color Ramsey number of the $j$-diamond is at most $jk$. Colorings of the Boolean lattice that assign sets of the same size the same color provide matching lower bounds for $j \in… — Tom Bohman, Will Cong, Quentin Dubroff, Teresa Huang, Zheyuan Li, BangTam Ngo — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Improved Sidorenko bound for hypergraph Turan densities
item.description: For every fixed integer $r\ge3$, we prove that the Turán density of every $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $m\ge1$ edges satisfies $π(F)\le1-c_rm^{-(r-1)/r}$, where $c_r>0$ depends only on $r$. This improves Sidorenko's general bound, whose gap from $1$ is of order $m^{-1}$. Complete $r$-uniform hypergraphs show that the exponent $(r-1)/r$ is optimal. The proof combines a potential argument for partial embeddings with the Lovász Local Lemma. — Shuyan Chen, Xinmin Hou, Xizhi Liu — arXiv: lean

item.title: The logarithmic exponent of the Ramsey number $r(4,t)$
item.description: We prove that $r(4,t) \ge \frac{t^3}{(\log t)^{2+o(1)}}$. This improves the lower bound of Mattheus and Verstraëte (Ann. of Math., 2024) by a factor of $(\log t)^{2-o(1)}$. — Qizhong Lin, Qiuyang Zhang — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
item.description: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly improving on long-horizon scientific and olympiad tasks. Recent systems have produced a Lean-formalized resolution of the Navier--Stokes problem and autonomous solutions to four open questions in the Erdős Conjectures database. Yet neither system releases both its underlying model and complete inference stack. More broadly, a single agent session remains brittle on difficult problems: early errors can propagate, missing domain knowledge can stall progress, and… — Zhengyang Zhang, Jing Xiong, Hongzhou Lin, Juihui Chung, Zijian Zhang, Song Han — arXiv: lean / arXiv: navier

item.title: Universal Radial Laws for Random Polynomials: Erdős Problem #522 and Non-Universal Fluctuations
item.description: We resolve Erdős Problem #522, posed in 1961, by proving that for random Littlewood polynomials the proportion of zeros in the closed unit disk converges almost surely to $1/2$. More generally, for partial sums of random power series with i.i.d. coefficients that are bounded, nondegenerate, and centrally symmetric, real Gaussian, or circular complex Gaussian, we prove that the proportion of zeros in the disk of radius $1+x/n$ converges almost surely to $\frac12(1+\coth x-1/x)$, uniformly in $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Thus… — Sebastien Kawada — arXiv: lean

item.title: Aspects of automatic continuity
item.description: Christian Rosendal and Luis Carlos Suarez Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 63 (), 637-684. Abstract, references and article information — Bulletin of the AMS

item.title: On the asymptotics of the Erdős-Rogers function
item.description: The Erdős-Rogers function $f_{\ell,s}(n)$ is the largest order of a $K_\ell$-free induced subgraph guaranteed to exist in every $K_s$-free graph on $n$ vertices. While this function is well understood for $s=\ell+1$, the case where $s$ is much larger than $\ell$ has remained wide open. A long-standing lower bound of Sudakov states that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\geq n^{\frac{\ell}{2s}+O_\ell(s^{-2})}$, while a recent result of Bradač shows that $f_{\ell,s}(n)\leq n^{\frac{\ell-1}{s-1}+o(1)}$. In this paper, we close this gap… — Domagoj Bradač, Oliver Janzer, Rik Sarkar — arXiv: ramsey

item.title: The Burr-Erdős-Graham-Sós conjecture for the seven-cycle
item.description: For a graph $H$, let $f(n,e,H)$ be the least number of colors in an edge-coloring of some $n$-vertex graph with at least $e$ edges in which every copy of $H$ is rainbow. Burr, Erdős, Graham, and Sós conjectured that $f(n,\lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1,C_{2k+1})=(1/8+o(1))n^2$ for every fixed $k\ge3$, and Bucić, Chen, and Ma recently proved this for all $k\ge4$. We prove the remaining case $k=3$: \[ f\left(n,\left\lfloor n^2/4\right\rfloor+1,C_7\right) =\left(\frac18+o(1)\right)n^2. \] The lower bound rests on a weighted… — Asad Shahab — arXiv: lean

item.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
item.description: Understanding nonlinear dynamics is central to many fields of study, yet most nonlinear systems are beyond the reach of closed-form solutions. Numerical simulation is then used to reveal dynamical structures before their existence can be established. This alone, however, leaves the validity of the computed solution unanswered. Rigorous numerical methods address this gap by combining computation with explicit analytic estimates. Among them, the radii polynomial approach, a Newton--Kantorovich type argument, turns… — Fengyang Wang, Konstantin Mischaikow, Marcio Gameiro — arXiv: additive / arXiv: lean

item.title: Another proof that the two color bipartite Ramsey number is $O(2^t)$
item.description: For positive integers $t$ and $q$ let $b_q(t)$ be the smallest integer $n$ so that any coloring of the edges of the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$ with $q$ colors yields a monochromatic copy of $K_{t,t}$. item.title: Optimally pseudorandom $K_4$-free graphs
item.description: We show that optimally pseudorandom $K_4$-free graphs of order $n$ and degree $d = Θ(n^{4/5})$ exist by constructing a graph in the split Cayley hexagon, matching the known upper bound. item.description: A wiring diagram is an arrangement of $m$ pseudolines, every two of which cross exactly once. item.description: Godsil, Roberson, Šámal and Severini conjectured that the quantum chromatic number of the categorical product of two graphs equals the minimum of the quantum chromatic numbers of the factors. item.title: On the multicolour Ramsey numbers $R(3,3,k)$
item.description: In this paper we determine the Ramsey number $R(3,3,k)$ up to a constant factor, showing that $$R(3,3,k) = Θ\bigg( \frac{k^3}{(\log k)^2} \bigg).$$ The proof of the lower bound combines the Hefty-Horn-King-Pfender construction for $R(3,k)$ with the method of Alon and Rödl.
